correctness.rationale: For a unit greedy basis vector \(p\), the source PSB formula gives exactly \(R^+=(I-pp^T)R(I-pp^T)\) for \(R=G-A\). Orthogonality makes the coordinate projectors commute, proving the mask formula after any selected set. Positive semidefiniteness of \(R_0=LI-A\) makes a zero diagonal deficit equivalent to an already exact basis direction. These facts prove both necessity and sufficiency of exactly \(s\) nontrivial updates. On a quadratic, the source Hessian-variation correction has \(M=0\), so scheme (36) contributes \(t+1\) updates per completed outer iteration and yields the stated ceiling formula. The diagonal example proves sharpness of the subsequent exact-Newton-step count.

value.rationale: The source's main algorithmic novelty is its multiple greedy PSB refinement, so identifying exactly what those extra refinements buy on the canonical quadratic model is a directly motivated question. The result separates two costs that the asymptotic rate alone does not: batching can reduce outer primal solves by a factor up to \(t+1\), yet it cannot reduce the total number \(s\) of nontrivial PSB Hessian updates. The sharp cutoff and predetermined ordering provide a reusable finite-complexity interpretation of the method rather than an arbitrary special-case calculation.
